successors.name: Neo-Assyrian Empire
successors.text: Bit Adini on the Euphrates south of Carchemish

ledger.x: c. 1000 BC: Bit Adini is established. The infobox gives "c. 1000 BC"; the page gives no founding event or founder and describes "an Aramaean state that existed as an independent kingdom" with its capital at Til Barsip (Tell Ahmar). The land is my reading.
857/856 BC: Bit Adini falls to Shalmaneser III.

wars.name: Ahuni and the conquest of Bit Adini
wars.outcome: "Ahuni of Bit Adini resisted for several years, but he surrendered to Shalmaneser in the winter of 857/856 BCE."

certainty.note: No frontier on the pages: the state is a circle at its capital.
